issues.description: HAS_TIME regex needs a comment naming the invariant it enforces as a pre-filter.
issues.detail: The /\dm?s/i guard is an unstated second specification of "contains a time token" that must stay in lockstep with the authoritative valueParser walk. A one-line comment naming it as a cheap pre-filter for valueParser — and noting that future time-unit additions must update both sites — would protect the abstraction and save the next maintainer time.

issues.description: No regression test pins the early-return behavior against false negatives.
issues.detail: The optimization is behavior-preserving in theory, but nothing guards against the regex accidentally rejecting a real violation (odd whitespace, case, vendor-prefixed value). A single targeted test exercising the early-return path would lock the invariant in and catch drift if the regex or unit set evolves.

issues.description: Performance claim ships with no benchmark numbers in the changeset.
issues.detail: The changeset frames this as a perf fix but provides no before/after measurements. For a hot-path optimization, brief timing numbers — or at least a note on the workload that motivated it — would justify the added complexity and let future maintainers evaluate whether the pre-filter still earns its keep.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on ACCEPT: a small, scoped, behavior-preserving optimization that short-circuits valueParser when the declaration value cannot contain a CSS time token. No reviewer found a correctness bug — the authoritative parser still runs whenever the cheap regex matches. The consensus asks for three light touch-ups before landing: a one-line comment naming the HAS_TIME regex as a pre-filter and its invariant, a regression test pinning the early-return path, and benchmark numbers in the changeset to justify the perf framing. Land with trivial fixups.
